subject: Dedicated capacity: bench results + pricing ask (GPU sizing & reserved commits)
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex.li@acme.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated sizing question + preliminary TPS numbers

Hi Rafael / Monica,

Quick context: we run a customer-facing inference pipeline (doc parsing + chat) that averages ~18 reqs/s during peak and spikes to ~120 reqs/s for short bursts when batch jobs complete. Latency we need is 95th <= 250ms for single-turn chat at ~1k token averages. We ran a quick local load test (attached) and saw KV cache hit patterns that look bursty.

We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated because we need predictable throughput and compliance controls. Before we move to a contract conversation, can you confirm the RD dedicated sizing (GPU pool) you recommend to hit sustained 150 TPS with 99.9% uptime and a 95th latency SLO of 250ms? Also curious how reserved commits vs monthly usage would be priced and whether there's a play for a commit discount if we sign a 12-month reserved commit.

Attached: acme_local_stress_summary.txt (small) — I can share more detailed traces if it helps.

Thanks,
Alex Li
Head of Platform
Acme AI

Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question + preliminary TPS numbers

Hi Alex — thanks for the details and the attached summary. This is exactly the right next step.

High level answers up front: yes, we can guarantee sustained throughput in the 150 TPS class with Dedicated by sizing a GPU pool appropriately and applying throughput SLAs tied to reserved capacity. The exact GPU count depends on your typical sequence lengths, model choice, and KV cache hit rate.

What we'll do next:
- Our infra team will run a Redwood-hosted load test against a model variant you plan to serve (can you confirm model name + quantization profile?).
- We'll provision a temporary dedicated pool (isolated test pool) that mirrors a 12x A100 setup and run a 24-hour soak + burst window to observe tail latencies.
- We'll share TPS traces, dashboard snapshots, and a sizing recommendation (GPU count + expected tokens/sec).

Can you confirm the model (or share a small model artifact) and whether your 120 reqs/s bursts are roughly 20k tokens/s or more? That helps pick batch sizes and kernel paths.

I'll loop in Vivek to run the tests and Monica to coordinate procurement/contracting language (reserved commits / discount tiers).

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question + preliminary TPS numbers

Rafael / Monica — we ran the Redwood-hosted tests 2026-02-16 to emulate Acme workload. Summary notes and artifacts attached.

Quick findings (high level):
- Model: open-llama-13B (quantized int8) — test used same token distribution supplied by Acme.
- Pool config used: 6x A100-80GB (single node inference per GPU), continuous batching enabled, KV prefix caching with 60s TTL.
- Sustained throughput: 160 TPS (single-turn, ~1k tokens) with 95th latency = 210ms.
- Burst handling: simulated 120 -> 300 TPS spike window using traffic shaping; we saw graceful degradation with prioritized routing (latency rose to 420ms at peak but recovered within 90s).
- Observability: attached ri_tps_dashboard_snapshot.png and kv_trace_sample.log for a representative burst sweep.

Sizing recommendation: for Acme's stated SLA (sustained 150 TPS @ 95th <= 250ms) we recommend Dedicated pool = 6x A100 with reserved commit of 2,500 GPU hours/month (this maps to a 75% utilization buffer for bursts). If Acme expects 2x growth in 12 months, plan to add +3 GPUs on a staggered rollout.

Price/packaging implications:
- Reserved commit (12mo) gives a 25% off list on Dedicated hourly rates + additional 10% contract-level credit for billing predictability.
- Monthly on-demand Dedicated is available but higher unit cost (~+40%).
- We can add an SLA clause for throughput with credits: if sustained throughput falls below 98% of committed capacity for >6 hours in a month, we apply a credit pro-rated to the impacted GPU hours. Language draft to follow.

Artifacts attached: acme_stress_report_20260216.pdf (full test), ri_tps_dashboard_snapshot.png, kv_trace_sample.log.

Ping me if you want deeper kernel-level traces.

- Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@acme.ai>

Subject: Proposed Dedicated package & pricing for Acme (6x A100)

Alex — thanks again for the quick turnaround. Vivek's team completed the tests and recommends a 6x A100 Dedicated pool to meet your 150 TPS @ 95th <= 250ms target. Key points below and an initial commercial outline.

Sizing: 6x A100-80GB Dedicated pool (isolated), continuous batching + KV caching configured per the attached tests.
SLA: Throughput SLO — 98% of committed capacity monthly; 95th latency SLO — 250ms (single-turn, 1k tokens). Failure credit model to be included in contract.
Pricing options:
- Option A (12-month reserved): 25% off hourly Dedicated list + additional 10% contract credit. Estimated monthly committed spend: $XX,XXX (we'll provide exact HubSpot quote).
- Option B (6-month reserved): 15% off list.
- Option C (on-demand): no commit discount (higher unit rates).

We can also structure a stepped commit where pricing improves as committed GPU hours cross thresholds. If you can commit to >=9 GPUs average over 12 months, we'll extend an additional 7.5% price concession.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm model variant and the expected growth profile (1.0x / 1.5x / 2.0x in 12 months).
2) If the numbers look reasonable, Monica will issue a draft term sheet (HubSpot link below) and I can share a DocuSign for signatures.

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-RI-2026-0091
Drive artifacts: https://drive.google.com/file/d/ACME_STRESS_20260216

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Rafael — appreciate the thoroughness. The tests look good and the 6x A100 recommendation aligns with our internal expectations. Couple of asks before we sign:

1) Can Redwood provide a firm committed price per GPU-hour in writing (not a % off) so our finance team can compare to internal budgets?
2) Would Redwood be willing to move to a 30% discount at 12-month commit if we sign a 12 mo + agree to a 9 GPU average (instead of 6) from month 4 onward? We're trying to secure better unit economics for the contract.
3) Please confirm the exact SLA language for throughput credits (we need the term sheet to include the trigger thresholds and credit calculation example).

If you can send an updated term sheet with those specifics, we can accelerate procurement (we have internal legal review queued).

Thanks,
Alex

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed Dedicated package & pricing for Acme (6x A100) — updated proposal

Alex — great questions. We've run the numbers and can be responsive to your ask with a commercial trade: if Acme signs a 12-month reserved commit and commits to an average of 9 GPUs starting month 4, we can provide a 30% discount on GPU-hour list rates for the committed portion. Key clarifications below: 

- Firm price: $14.50 / GPU-hour (committed portion) after the 30% discount (list = $20.75 / GPU-hour). This will be reflected in the term sheet.
- Commit structure: 12-month contract; months 1–3 ramp to target; months 4–12 average of 9 GPUs to qualify for the 30% tier. If actual usage falls below the committed average, we reconcile at month-end and apply true-ups at the committed rate.
- SLA language (excerpt): "If sustained throughput (defined as rolling 1h windows aggregated across the Dedicated pool) falls below 98% of the committed capacity for more than 6 cumulative hours in a billing month, Redwood will issue a service credit equal to 1% of that month's committed Dedicated spend for every 6-hour block of impact, capped at 20% for the month." (we will include a worked example in the term sheet).

Attached are the updated term sheet and the full benchmark report. I'll ask Monica to open a DocuSign for the draft once you confirm the pricing tier.

Next steps: confirm the growth profile and whether you accept the ramp+9-GPU qualification. If yes, Monica will circulate the contract and we can target a March 1 start date.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
